messages.content:
You write one short block of text for the quality overall summary of a drug regulatory submission.

Rules you must follow:
A. Write in plain regulatory wording, short sentences, one statement each. Each sentence must follow one of the ALLOWED WORDINGS listed for it in the unit message; you choose which one.
B. Never write a digit, a number word, a degree sign, a percent sign or a unit. Every value is a placeholder from the FACTS list, written exactly as [[name]]. A placeholder already holds its own unit.
C. Use every placeholder under MUST MENTION, and only in the sentence where it belongs. Write each attribute name exactly as given, with its placeholder if it has one.
D. Add nothing that is not asked: no conclusion, no judgement, no cause, no trend, no source, no words such as stable, robust, meets or complies. The word demonstrated is allowed only when the line DEMONSTRATED says allowed.
E. Only the words that regulatory summaries normally use are accepted: for example proposed shelf life, stored at, excursions, permitted, stability, data cover, data are available, long-term conditions, accelerated conditions, ranged from, between, outside the limit, within the specification limits.
F. The demo label is exactly the words "In illustrative demonstration data," and the sentence goes on in lower case. Use it only where WHAT TO WRITE asks for it.
G. DEMONSTRATED: not allowed means the data do not support that word: say only that stability data cover, or data are available for, the periods.
H. Output only the text, as plain text.

UNIT: specification
TESTS, in this order: Dissolution, Impurity O, Impurity L, Total impurities
WHAT TO WRITE: the first line is one short sentence that starts with the demo label and introduces the table that follows; it names the drug product specification, its tests and their acceptance criteria, and it ends with a full stop. Then one line per test, in the order given: the test name, a colon, the limit kind, then the placeholder. No full stop after these lines.
FACTS:
- [[spec_dissolution_av]]: acceptance limit for Dissolution (NLT)
- [[spec_impurity_o]]: acceptance limit for Impurity O (NMT)
- [[spec_impurity_l]]: acceptance limit for Impurity L (NMT)
- [[spec_impurities_total]]: acceptance limit for Total impurities (NMT)
MUST MENTION: [[spec_dissolution_av]], [[spec_impurity_o]], [[spec_impurity_l]], [[spec_impurities_total]]
ALLOWED WORDINGS (use exactly one per sentence; write each <name> as the placeholder [[name]]; fill <attribute>, <condition word> and <test name> with the given words, copied exactly as given, with the same capital letters and without any < >; <limit> is the placeholder of that test; every sentence ends with a full stop except the test lines):
spec intro:
  - In illustrative demonstration data, the drug product specification lists <word-a> tests and acceptance criteria.
  - In illustrative demonstration data, the drug product specification below lists <word-b> tests and their acceptance criteria.
  (<word-a> is the word these; <word-b> is the word the)
spec row:
  - <test name>: <NMT or NLT> <limit>
  - <test name> <NMT or NLT> <limit>

text:
In illustrative demonstration data, the drug product specification below lists these tests and their acceptance criteria.
Dissolution: NLT [[spec_dissolution_av]]
Impurity O: NMT [[spec_impurity_o]]
Impurity L: NMT [[spec_impurity_l]]
Total impurities: NMT [[spec_impurities_total]]
problems: (c) sentence 1: unrecognised: it fits none of the allowed sentence wordings

UNIT: public
DEMONSTRATED: allowed
WHAT TO WRITE: three sentences without the demo label, in this order: first the proposed shelf life with the storage temperature range; second the permitted temperature excursions; third how long data cover long-term conditions and accelerated conditions.
FACTS:
- [[accel]]: months of accelerated data
- [[ex_high]]: highest permitted excursion temperature
- [[ex_low]]: lowest permitted excursion temperature
- [[long]]: months of long-term data
- [[shelf]]: proposed shelf life in months
- [[st_high]]: highest storage temperature
- [[st_low]]: lowest storage temperature
MUST MENTION: [[shelf]], [[st_low]], [[st_high]], [[ex_low]], [[ex_high]], [[long]], [[accel]]
ALLOWED WORDINGS (use exactly one per sentence; write each <name> as the placeholder [[name]]; fill <attribute>, <condition word> and <test name> with the given words, copied exactly as given, with the same capital letters and without any < >; <limit> is the placeholder of that test; every sentence ends with a full stop except the test lines):
shelf:
  - The proposed shelf life is <shelf> when stored at <st_low> to <st_high>.
  - When stored at <st_low> to <st_high>, the proposed shelf life is <shelf>.
excursion:
  - Excursions are permitted from <ex_low> to <ex_high>.
  - Temperature excursions between <ex_low> and <ex_high> are permitted.
study:
  - Stability was demonstrated for <long> at long-term conditions and <accel> at accelerated conditions.
  - Stability data cover <long> at long-term conditions and <accel> at accelerated conditions.
  - Long-term stability was demonstrated for <long>, and accelerated stability for <accel>.
  - Data are available for <long> at long-term conditions and <accel> at accelerated conditions.
  - Long-term data are available for <long>, and accelerated data for <accel>.

text:
The proposed shelf life is [[shelf]] when stored at [[st_low]] to [[st_high]].
Temperature excursions between [[ex_low]] and [[ex_high]] are permitted.
Data are available for [[long]] at long-term conditions and [[accel]] at accelerated conditions.
